corePages.headline: In der Konditorei
corePages.bodyGerman:
Guten Tag! Was darf es sein?

Einen Kaffee mit Milch, bitte.

Sonst noch etwas?

Ja, ein Stück Käsekuchen. Was kostet das?

Das macht zusammen sieben Euro fünfzig.
corePages.bodyEnglish:
Good day! What would you like?

A coffee with milk, please.

Anything else?

Yes, a piece of cheesecake. How much is that?

That comes to seven euros fifty.
corePages.culturalTip: Ordering is one of the few situations where Germans stay formal — 'Sie' with a shopkeeper is normal even in a small village café.

corePages.headline: Essen & Trinken
corePages.bodyEnglish: The words you need to survive a menu.

corePages.headline: Einen, bitte — der Akkusativ
corePages.bodyGerman:
der Kaffee  →  einen Kaffee     (masculine shifts)
die Milch   →  eine Milch      (feminine stays)
das Wasser  →  ein Wasser      (neuter stays)
corePages.bodyEnglish: When a masculine noun is the thing you WANT (the direct object), 'der' becomes 'den' and 'ein' becomes 'einen'. Feminine and neuter don't change. This is the accusative case — you already use it every time you order something.
corePages.culturalTip: 'Einen Kaffee, bitte' is so common it works as a full sentence. Drop the verb entirely — Germans do.

corePages.headline: Bestellen
corePages.bodyGerman:
Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.

Ich hätte gern einen Tee mit Zitrone.
corePages.bodyEnglish: 'Ich möchte' (I would like) is the polite workhorse of every order. 'Ich hätte gern' is a notch more formal and sounds perfectly natural — either is safe.

grammar.explanationEnglish: The accusative case marks the thing you act ON. Only masculine nouns change: 'der' → 'den', 'ein' → 'einen', 'kein' → 'keinen'. Feminine, neuter and plural look identical to the nominative. Order anything masculine and you've used the accusative.
grammar.englishBridge: English lost its cases, so there's nothing to compare — just memorise the masculine flip. 'A coffee' as a customer is ALWAYS 'einen Kaffee'.
grammar.commonMistake: 'ein Kaffee' ✗ when ordering → 'einen Kaffee' ✓. Masculine is the only gender that shifts.
grammar.targetSentenceEnglish: I would like a coffee, please.

writing.promptEnglish: Build: 'Ich möchte einen Tee mit Zitrone.'

practice.explanationEnglish: 'der Kaffee' is masculine, and as the thing you want it shifts to the accusative: 'einen Kaffee'.
'Stück' is neuter, so the article stays 'ein': 'Ein Stück Kuchen'. Serving sizes come before the noun.

practice.prompt: Which stays unchanged in the accusative?
practice.explanationEnglish: Only masculine shifts. 'die Milch' is feminine, so it stays 'eine Milch'.
